blocks.text: Condo buildings in Durieu

Every listing for this ground carries a "Mission" mailing address, and SnapStats groups the "Durieu" sub-area under the board community Mission for reporting only — but Durieu is an unincorporated farming community in Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area F, in the Hatzic Valley north of Hatzic Prairie. The FVRD's Electoral Areas Housing Needs Report lists "Electoral Area F: McConnell Creek, Hatzic Prairie" and states the Hatzic Valley includes the historic settlement areas of Hatzic Prairie, Durieu, Miracle Valley and McConnell Creek. Rural taxes here are paid to the Province under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act (5% after July 2, further 5% after October 31). Western fringe: feed cards on Stave Lake Road sit toward the valley's western edge, near where Area F meets the City of Mission boundary — which side of the line a specific Stave Lake Road parcel sits on is UNVERIFIED at parcel level; check the PID before quoting City or rural rules for one of those listings. The board's grouping of a "Durieu" sub-area under Mission is a reporting grouping only and is not quoted as a Durieu market figure.
Streets, schools and getting around Durieu

items.t: The page headed "Durieu Homes for Sale | Mission Acreages & Rural" showed 13 results at reading — a snapshot, not a market statistic. Every first-page card is labelled board sub-area "Durieu" with a "Mission" mailing address, on streets including Sylvester Road, Stave Lake Road, Farms Road, Sward Road, Seux Road and Durieu Road; the page covers the farming community of Durieu in the Hatzic Valley, north of Hatzic Prairie — it does NOT cover land inside the City of Mission, despite the mailing addresses.

The valley, per the FVRD: almost all Area F residents live in the southwest of the area covered by the Electoral Area F – Hatzic Valley Official Community Plan, between the northern shore of Hatzic Lake and the southern shore of Stave Lake; the valley is accessed by Stave Lake Road from the west, connecting to Mission, and by Sylvester Road from Electoral Area G to the south; the majority of the inhabited area is within the Agricultural Land Reserve, with active commercial and hobby farming in addition to sparse residential uses.

Planning and zoning framework: FVRD official community plan and zoning bylaws govern this ground (the Hatzic Valley OCP covers the inhabited valley), but the specific OCP/zoning bylaw numbers and zone names applying to Durieu lots are UNVERIFIED in the research pass — no FVRD bylaw document for Area F was opened, and the "RU36" zone label in one feed card is listing text only. Confirm with the FVRD for the PID.

Flood history: the FVRD's Area F history records that a flood in 1948 broke a dyke along Hatzic Lake, the lake grew five times in size to 25 km², and the Hatzic Prairie was largely under water. A specific Durieu property's current flood status, dyke protection and flood-construction requirements: UNVERIFIED at parcel level.

School-district coverage (SD75) and local governance are different things — SD75 serves this FVRD community even though the City of Mission does not govern it. Catchment schools for any specific Durieu address are UNVERIFIED — no catchment document was opened and no locator run is on record.

Servicing (water/sewer vs well/septic) for Durieu lots: UNVERIFIED at parcel level — feed listing text repeatedly references drilled wells, public water at a lot line, creeks and artesian wells, which is listing copy only. Transit and commute: no TransLink or BC Transit service summary for Durieu was opened, and no official source states commute times in minutes (feed time claims are listing copy): UNVERIFIED. Health care: Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd Street, Mission, consists of a 25-bed medical inpatient unit, a 20-bed PATH unit and a 10-bed Christine Morrison Hospice, and provides primary acute care, outpatient and inpatient services, general medicine, laboratory and diagnostic services; travel time from a Durieu property: UNVERIFIED.

items.t: Secondary suites in Area F have a hard shape limit: the FVRD records significant limits on development options in Electoral Area F with the majority of lands in the ALR, and that secondary suites are freely permitted with no restrictions related to farm use, but must be located within the principal dwelling and could not be a separate detached structure, such as a garden suite, or a multi-unit structure for farm workers. City of Mission suite rules (registration, the $63 annual fee) do NOT apply here.

ALR housing and stratification rules: parcel-level ALR status is per address: UNVERIFIED — first-page feed text itself puts one Durieu Road parcel in the ALR and states roughly 18 acres of a Seux Road parcel are NOT in the ALR, both as listing claims to verify on the ALC maps by PID. Where land is in the ALR: one principal residence capped at 500 m² total floor area, plus at most one additional detached residence up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger parcels; a secondary suite only if entirely contained within the principal residence and local bylaws permit suites; landowners who wish to subdivide must apply under the Agricultural Land Commission Act and secure ALC approval; and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; a strata plan deposit is a subdivision — Strata Property Act s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)).

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), for comparison product only: no park is verified in Durieu; where a buyer compares a valley park home instead, the MHPTA rent-increase limit is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027 — confirmed from the park's own tenancy documents for any specific pad.

blocks.text: Good to know about Durieu

items.t: School district and municipality part company here.

A detached garden suite is not the Area F suite route. In Electoral Area F a secondary suite must sit within the principal dwelling; a separate detached structure such as a garden suite does not qualify as the suite — the only detached second-residence route is the ALC additional-residence frame on ALR land (90 m² or 186 m² by parcel size), subject to FVRD zoning as well.

Most of the inhabited valley is farm-reserve land. The FVRD records that the majority of the inhabited Hatzic Valley area is within the Agricultural Land Reserve, with active commercial and hobby farming alongside sparse residential uses — so the ALR housing caps and the stratification bar, not city suite or strata rules, are the working frame for most Durieu purchases.

The western fringe needs a PID check before any rule is quoted. Feed cards on Stave Lake Road sit near where Area F meets the City of Mission boundary — the one place on this page where the City frame could actually apply to a single parcel. Which side a specific parcel sits on is UNVERIFIED in this research.

There is no Durieu market statistic to hide behind. No SnapStats figure is quoted for this FVRD community and no sub-area median exists in the research record — pricing a Durieu acreage is comparable-by-comparable work on the property's own evidence, not a median lookup.

faq.q: How did Durieu sell in September 2026?
faq.a: It recorded no sales in the permitted source: the sub-area showed 3 detached listings with 0 sold and 0 Condos & Townhomes listings with 0 sold, so no sales ratio or sub-area median exists for the month; the Mission board-community medians (detached $814,000; attached $430,000) are board context for a different market, not Durieu figures (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Can I add a suite or a second home on a Durieu acreage?
faq.a: Two gates apply. In FVRD Electoral Area F, a secondary suite must be located within the principal dwelling — a separate detached structure such as a garden suite is not the suite route — and if the parcel is in the ALR, an additional detached residence is limited to 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha) on top of one principal residence of at most 500 m²; confirm both the FVRD zoning and the parcel's ALR status for the specific PID before relying on a second-dwelling plan.

faq.q: Are there any condos in Durieu?
faq.a: None verified — no condo building in this community was confirmed on an official, developer or strata source in the research or in fresh checks, and no townhome complex was confirmed either. The verified stock is acreage houses, vacant land and farm packages. A buyer who wants a Mission condo is buying inside the City of Mission, documented in the city condo notes — not in Durieu.

No. Listings carry Mission mailing addresses and the board groups the sub-area under Mission, but Durieu is an unincorporated FVRD Electoral Area F community in the Hatzic Valley — the FVRD's housing-needs report places Durieu among the Hatzic Valley settlement areas of Electoral Area F — and the City of Mission does not govern it.

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to on a Durieu property, and what is the penalty?
faq.a: The Province: rural-area properties receive their tax notice from the Surveyor of Taxes Office and pay the Province, not the FVRD or a municipality; rural taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid on October 31 (Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s. 11) — not Mission's flat 10%.

faq.q: Can an ALR farm property here be bought or created as a strata condo?
faq.a: No — ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)), and ALR subdivision needs Commission permission. A Durieu farm listing is a house on land under the ALC residence frame, not condo stock, whatever a feed label suggests.
